pages.text: Kofi had a little patch of soil behind his house. ‘I will make a garden,’ he said. Maame gave him some seeds.
sentences: Kofi had a little patch of soil behind his house.
‘I will make a garden,’ he said.
Maame gave him some seeds.
pages.alt: A boy looks at a small patch of brown soil behind a house while his mother hands him a paper packet of seeds.

pages.text: Kofi dug little holes. He put one seed in each hole and covered it with soil. Then he gave the soil a drink of water.
sentences: Kofi dug little holes.
He put one seed in each hole and covered it with soil.
Then he gave the soil a drink of water.
pages.alt: Kofi kneels and drops a seed into a small hole, with a watering can beside him.

pages.text: One day passed. Two days passed. Three days passed. Nothing came up. ‘Maybe the seeds are sleeping,’ said Kofi.
sentences: One day passed.
Two days passed.
Three days passed.
Nothing came up.
‘Maybe the seeds are sleeping,’ said Kofi.
pages.alt: Kofi looks closely at flat soil with his chin on his hands.

pages.text: Kofi did not give up. Every morning he watered the soil and sang a little song. Then, one morning, he saw something small and green!
sentences: Kofi did not give up.
Every morning he watered the soil and sang a little song.
Then, one morning, he saw something small and green!
pages.alt: Kofi sings while watering; a tiny green sprout pushes through the soil.

pages.text: Soon the garden grew tall. There were three red tomatoes. There were two green okra pods. ‘So many colours!’ said Kofi.
sentences: Soon the garden grew tall.
There were three red tomatoes.
There were two green okra pods.
‘So many colours!’ said Kofi.
pages.alt: A garden with three bright red tomatoes and two green okra pods on their plants.

pages.text: There were four yellow corn cobs. There were five orange carrots poking out of the soil. Kofi counted them all, one, two, three, four, five.
sentences: There were four yellow corn cobs.
There were five orange carrots poking out of the soil.
Kofi counted them all, one, two, three, four, five.
pages.alt: Four yellow corn cobs on tall stalks and five orange carrot tops showing in the soil.

pages.text: Kofi picked a basket of vegetables for Maame. ‘Look, Maame, my garden has red, green, yellow and orange!’
sentences: Kofi picked a basket of vegetables for Maame.
‘Look, Maame, my garden has red, green, yellow and orange!’
pages.alt: Kofi proudly holds up a basket of colourful vegetables to his smiling mother.

pages.text: That night they cooked a big pot of soup with the vegetables. Kofi smiled. ‘Waiting was hard, but it was worth it.’ The end.
sentences: That night they cooked a big pot of soup with the vegetables.
Kofi smiled.
‘Waiting was hard, but it was worth it.’ The end.
pages.alt: Kofi and his mother share a bowl of soup at a table by candlelight.

activities.question: What did Kofi do when nothing came up?
activities.explanation: Kofi did not give up. He watered the soil every morning.

activities.prompt: What happened first, next and last?
items: A small green sprout came up.
Kofi picked a basket of vegetables.

activities.prompt: Which words start with the c sound?
Is there something you waited for that was hard to wait for? How did you feel?

glossary.definition: The brown earth where plants grow.
Tiny parts of a plant that grow into new plants.
A long green vegetable used in soups and stews.
A container woven from dry grass or reeds.
